key_insight: Hard–soft domain interaction accelerates low-cycle fatigue failure in friction stir welded aluminum joints by localizing cyclic plastic strain in the softened heat-affected zone and promoting fatigue–ratcheting damage.
engineering_relevance: Fatigue assessment of friction stir welded joints should account for deformation mismatch between the softened heat-affected zone and neighboring harder regions.
method: Characterize precipitates across heterogeneous weld regions.
Use macroscopic digital image correlation to track deformation under cyclic loading.
Relate strain localization, back stress, and compressive ratcheting to fatigue failure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pronounced cyclic plastic strain localization and crack initiation in the heat-affected zone, alongside back stress and Bauschinger-effect-driven compressive ratcheting, but provides no quantitative fatigue-life results.
watch_item: Applicability to other alloys, weld conditions, and loading histories requires validation beyond the reported joints.
paper_title: Hard domain–soft domain interaction facilitating LCF failure in friction stir welding joints with macroscopic heterogeneity
